washers.landing_share_min.measured_on: decided: the full ring, less the sampling error of the probe
washers.landing_share_min.description: share of the washer ring that must lie on material

washers.landing_gap_max.description: a washer farther than this from its landing does not lie on it

washers.slot_land_min.measured_on: decided, nobody measured it: an M3 washer D7 over a slot 3.4 wide has 1.8 on each flank, over a slot 5 wide it has 1.0
washers.slot_land_min.description: width of washer ring that lies on each flank of a slot the washer bridges: half of the washer diameter less the slot width

washers.spot_face_clearance.measured_on: decided: a 12 mm washer in a 13.2 mm spot face (0.6 nozzle, PETG-CF, one printer); 13.0 was used before and is superseded
washers.spot_face_clearance.description: a spot face is wider than the washer by at least this much

washers.gap_to_neighbour.measured_on: decided after round washers hit a motor body in a model; 0.1 was accepted once at one flat
washers.gap_to_neighbour.description: gap from a washer and its screw head to the nearest body that is not what they clamp

washers.ref_pattern.measured_on: naming habit of one project; set it to how washer refs are named. A ref the pattern does not match is not checked at all
washers.ref_pattern.description: a body whose own name matches is a washer (it must be a thin ring); a body with no hardware word in its own name whose component's name matches is one only when it is a ring of the washers table

washers.ring_overlap_min.measured_on: decided, never confirmed or measured: about 2 mm of a 12 mm washer over the ring it clamps
washers.ring_overlap_min.description: radial overlap of a clamp washer over its own bearing ring

washers.clamp_thickness_min.measured_on: computed, not tested: a 1.0 mm washer yields from about 15 to 35 N*m of tipping on one base joint
washers.clamp_thickness_min.description: thickness of a washer in a clamp that carries tipping, unless it is hardened

rules.title: A washer lies on its landing
rules.statement: Every washer lies on material over at least {washers.landing_share_min} of its ring, within {washers.landing_gap_max}, in its real seated position and at its measured outer diameter. The ring is counted outside the opening the washer sits over (its screw hole, a pocket mouth with its relief). A washer over a slot of the part bears on the two flanks of the slot: it passes when it reaches at least {washers.slot_land_min} over each flank and its ring is on material everywhere beside the slot. It fails when a flank is missing, and when the slot is nearly as wide as the washer. A spot face is at least {washers.spot_face_clearance} wider than the washer. A clamp washer on a bearing ring is the one washer that bridges: it bears on its ring, and everything else under it stays at least {bearings.clamp_room_washer} below its face. A clamp washer reaches at least {washers.ring_overlap_min} over its ring, or the whole face of that ring where the ring offers less (the outer ring (D - Da_max) / 2, the inner one (da_min - d) / 2, from the bearings table), within {bearings.contact_gap_max}, and no further over its ring than where the shield or seal begins (outer ring to D2, inner ring to d1, from "shields" of the bearings table): further on it presses the shield. A bearing whose shield the table does not give is not judged there when its washer reaches past the ISO face of the ring.
rules.why: Six clamp washers landed on plastic beside the ring they were meant to clamp, once print shrink had used up a 0.3 mm set-back. A washer heeled on the edge of a spot face.
fix_order: Move the screw so the whole ring lies on the landing.
Use the washer size of the table that fits.
A clamp washer: set the landing beside the ring back by the clamp room.
rules.note: A clamp washer is known by the bearing ref it bears on. What its ring must touch and miss on the bearing side is in bearings.holding and bearings.clamp_room; this rule is the washer's own view of the same set-back. A raised melt ring under a washer is not seen here: inserts.relief_missing owns every pocket without a relief, in a spot face too.

rules.title: A washer and its head clear the neighbours
rules.statement: A washer with its screw head keeps at least {washers.gap_to_neighbour} to every body it does not clamp. The stack stands proud by the washer thickness plus the head height: 2.65 for a 1.0 washer under an M3 button head, 3.15 for a 1.5 washer. Where a fixed part is nearer than that, washer and head are sunk flush or the stationary part gets a groove.
rules.why: Round washers hit a motor body in a model. Where a stationary plate stood 1.0 from the clamped face, a stack 2.65 proud had no room and was sunk flush.
fix_order: Counterbore the washer and the head flush.
Use a flat-sided or smaller washer.
rules.note: Checked in the pose as modelled. The same gap over the whole travel of a joint is a sweep: clearance.sweep_full_travel, deferred.

rules.title: A clamp washer touches only its own ring
rules.statement: A clamp washer overlaps its own bearing ring by about {washers.ring_overlap_min} and touches nothing else: not the other ring, not the seal, no fixed part. It is modelled at its measured outer diameter, in its real seated position, and checked like a part. Its spot face is wider than the washer, and the floor of the spot face is set back from the ring face by the clamp room.
rules.why: Round washers hit a motor body in the model and became flat-sided or shifted washers. Six washers of one clamp landed on plastic in a built joint.
rules.note: The parts a script checks are washers.landing (the lap over its ring, at least and at most: a washer that reaches the shield fails there), washers.proud, bearings.holding and bearings.clamp_room.

rules.title: Washer thickness follows the load
rules.statement: Where a washer clamp carries tipping, the washers are at least {washers.clamp_thickness_min} thick or hardened. The thicker washer stands 0.5 more proud: check washers.proud again.
rules.why: By calculation a 1.0 mm washer yields from about 15 to 35 N*m of tipping on a base joint. No bench test is on record.

rules.title: A washer landing is free of melt rings
rules.statement: A washer that heels on a landing with insert pockets needs that landing flat. Every pocket there has its melt relief, or its melt ring is shaved flush before the washer goes on, as a written bench step.
rules.why: Clamp-washer pockets close to a bearing seat keep no relief. Since the washers heel on that same landing, a ring left there tilts the washer, and neither a check nor a bench step covered it.
rules.note: See inserts.noroom_bench. The set-back of the landing behind the ring face is bearings.clamp_room: decided, until a print confirms that the washers pull flat.

rules.title: A head over a slot sits on a washer
rules.statement: A screw head over a slot or an oversize hole sits on a flat washer that spans it. A bare head bears on the two flanks of the slot only.
rules.why: No failed print behind it: a practice on belt-tension slots and adjustable mounts.

rules.title: Printed washers and shims need their own slicer settings
rules.statement: A printed washer, shim or ring narrower than two line widths ({target.line_width} each) is sliced with the Arachne wall generator and without X-Y hole compensation, set per object. Its thickness is a whole number of layers. Where that cannot be had, use a metal shim.
rules.why: Printed washers came out with an empty first layer.
rules.note: Found on the STL by walls.one_line.
